craft_notes: Sthāyin: resolve turning inward (the gaze taught). Sanskrit first: object (her), means (light kumbhaka), formula (sign pointed), pivot (raising beyond) → L4 sets gaze+means line 1, formula+pivot line 2. Rows: row 6 silent ('her' is IN the verse — no vocative invented). Rupture: colon after 'slight' — effort gentled, definition follows. Close: end-weight on the open door ('rite' — the practice-word, raising beyond it). Minimal pass: 'this rite' for ataḥ param (the beyond-rite; singable). Read aloud: line 1 softens (soft/slight), colon, line 2 firms (sign/raising). Rejected: 'hold your breath' — killed: manāk is slight, instruction must stay gentle; 'the next step' — killed: param is beyond, step imports stairs.

lines: Gaze on śakti — breath held soft and slight:
this is the sign, and raising waits beyond this rite.
l4.sanskrit_cite: tāmevālokayec chaktiṃ manāk kumbhakavṛttinā / etal lakṣaṇam uddiṣṭam utthāpanam ataḥ param

reads_against.argmap: Gazing at her with light breath-hold defines the sign; raising begins beyond it.
c1_essence: Sealed breath, steady gaze at śakti — the sign defined, raising beyond.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta strained toward bhayānaka (wonder edged with fear)
